files.purpose: A self-hosted main-thread hang detector: a dedicated background Thread pings the main queue every 0.5 s, and when no pong arrives for 4 s it shells out to /usr/bin/sample against its own pid and writes every thread's stack to a timestamped report under ~/Library/Logs/Droppy Code, keeping the 10 newest reports.

"

files.purpose: A generic two-generation (current/previous) cost-bounded cache struct used for thumbnails and other recent-item memories: hits in the previous generation are promoted into the current one, and when the current generation exceeds its count limit or cost budget it is demoted wholesale to previous and a fresh current is started.

platform_assumptions: Pure Swift value type; no Apple framework dependency beyond importing Foundation
feature_notes: Generational eviction rather than LRU: when current.count >= limit or currentCost > costLimit - cost, the whole current map becomes previous (dropping the old previous) and current is emptied and re-reserved to limit
A read that hits `previous` removes it from previous, subtracts its cost from previousCost, and re-inserts it into current, so recently used items survive the next rotation
An entry whose cost exceeds costLimit is rejected outright (guard cost <= costLimit else { return }), after the existing entry for that key has already been removed
insert() always calls removeValue(for:) first, so re-inserting a key never double-counts cost

contains() checks both generations; value(for:) has the promotion side effect and is therefore mutating
Effective capacity is up to 2x limit in terms of what can still be found, since previous entries remain readable

files.purpose: The incremental byte framer for child-process stdio, supporting two wire framings: newline-delimited messages and LSP-style Content-Length headers separated by CRLFCRLF, with a scan cursor so re-scanning is bounded and a finish() that flushes a trailing unterminated line.

platform_assumptions: Foundation Data slicing semantics; no macOS-specific API
feature_notes: Line framing splits on the single byte 0x0A (LF); the delimiter itself is not included in the returned message
Content-Length framing: the header block ends at the exact bytes \r\n\r\n; the header is UTF-8 decoded and scanned for a line whose name, trimmed of whitespace and lowercased, equals "content-length"
A header without a usable Content-Length (unparseable or negative) is skipped: contentLength returns nil and the loop continues past that header without emitting a message
The partial-header rewind is `search = max(start, buffer.endIndex - 3)`, so a separator split across reads is still found (3 bytes of the 4-byte separator may remain unscanned)
finish() returns the leftover buffer only in .lines framing and only when non-empty; in .contentLength framing a truncated body is dropped. It always resets buffer, scanned and bodyLength
After each append pass the buffer is re-based to `start` only when start moved, and `scanned` records the unsearched distance so bytes are not re-scanned from the beginning each read

ui_elements: Cache key format "<path>#<pixels>#<fillingSquare>" where pixels = max(1, Int((pointSize * 2).rounded(.up))), i.e. a fixed 2x point-to-pixel scale
feature_notes: A 2x scale factor is assumed for every request: pixels = max(1, Int((pointSize * 2).rounded(.up)))
fillingSquare mode enlarges the requested max pixel size by the aspect ratio max(w,h)/min(w,h), clamped to 2048 pixels, so a square crop is still filled at full resolution

Decode options: kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailFromImageAlways true, kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailWithTransform true (EXIF orientation applied), kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately true, kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize = pixels
Request coalescing: concurrent callers for the same key await the same Task; a caller giving up waits the decode out rather than cancelling it for the others (comment is explicit about this)
The in-flight entry is only cleared and the result only cached when inFlight[key] is still that same task, so a superseded decode does not evict a newer one
Cancellation: an early return of nil if Task.isCancelled on entry, and the result is discarded (returns nil) if the caller was cancelled by the time the decode finished
Cache cost is image.bytesPerRow * image.height in both caches, so the byte budgets are real decoded-bitmap bytes
The stated motivation is 15 thumbnails for the downloads popover decoding side by side instead of serially
unresolved_questions: Who writes into ThumbnailMemory (the view that stores a decoded CGImage after drawing it) is outside this bundle.
